items.title: Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end second day without a breakthrough
items.summary: US-mediated three-way talks in Abu Dhabi, with Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediating, ran a second and final scheduled day on 11 November. Kyiv and Washington called them constructive, and the sides discussed a large prisoner swap, but no breakthrough was reported and Russia's Lavrov rejected a truce.
items.why: A ceasefire or its absence shapes energy prices, European demand and the hiring outlook of firms exposed to the region.

items.title: Guterres calls for a 'climate justice pact' as COP31 leaders meet in Antalya
items.summary: The leaders' segment of COP31 opened in Antalya, Türkiye, on 11 November, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres urging a new climate justice pact and taxes on fossil fuel companies. Several big names are absent, including the US for a second year, and the presidency wants the talks to focus on implementing past pledges.
items.why: Climate commitments flow into ESG reporting, green jobs and sustainability roles that HR and marketing teams increasingly own.

items.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris amid uncertainty over US approach
items.summary: G7 top diplomats met in Paris on 9 November (three days ago) with visible differences on global crises, focusing on the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Questions centred on how US foreign policy will shift after the midterm elections.
items.why: G7 alignment on sanctions and trade affects multinational strategy and the global mobility of talent.

items.title: Republicans lose control of Congress in US midterms
items.summary: NPR reports that Republicans suffered severe losses and lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, with analysts linking the result partly to unpopular policies such as the Iran war. The shift is already colouring how allies read US foreign policy.
items.why: A divided Washington changes the odds on tariffs, visas and trade rules that drive offshoring and campus hiring in India.

items.title: Cabinet extends Stand-Up India scheme to 2031
items.summary: The Union Cabinet on 11 November extended the Stand-Up India scheme for five years to 31 March 2031, with a target of at least 2.5 lakh more beneficiaries. It also extended the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units to 2031 with a reported Rs 4,111 crore corpus.
items.why: Cheaper guaranteed credit for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs widens the small-business pipeline that marketing and HR services sell to.

items.title: Rs 62,370 crore fertiliser subsidy approved for rabi season
items.summary: The Cabinet approved a Rs 62,370 crore subsidy on phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for the 2026-27 rabi season, which Daily Pioneer says is 50 per cent higher than for kharif. The government said fertiliser stocks are comfortable.
items.why: Farm support sustains rural incomes, a key driver of FMCG and two-wheeler demand that rural marketing plans depend on.

items.title: October inflation, due today, expected to hit RBI's 6% ceiling
items.summary: MoSPI releases October CPI data on 12 November. Economist polls put it at about 6% (Mint range 5.9% to 6.2%, ICRA 6.1%), up from 5.54% in September; these are forecasts, not published data. A print above 6% would be the first breach of the RBI's upper limit since October 2024, after the MPC raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October.
items.why: Higher inflation and rates squeeze consumer spending and salary budgets, which shapes pricing, campaigns and compensation planning.

items.title: Sensex ends 773 points higher, Nifty at 25,255
items.summary: Indian benchmarks rose about 0.9% on 11 November after a market holiday, with the Sensex closing at 81,879.40 and the Nifty at 25,255.05 after paring early gains. Lower energy prices and a return of foreign fund inflows helped; PSU banks rose nearly 3% while IT and healthcare lagged.
items.why: Market mood feeds into IPO plans, campus hiring budgets and consumer confidence.

items.title: Strong Q2 earnings put Nifty within 5% of its record
items.summary: Business Standard reports that large caps are leading on stronger-than-expected September-quarter results, leaving benchmarks less than 5% below their lifetime highs. One broker estimates Nifty 50 earnings growth at 20% for the quarter (provisional).
items.why: Healthy earnings usually precede bigger hiring plans and marketing spends for the coming year.

items.title: Maersk to cut about 15% of corporate roles
items.summary: Moller-Maersk is cutting about 15% of its corporate roles across regions and headquarters, citing weaker earnings from lower freight rates and overcapacity in shipping, according to a layoffs tracker. The exact headcount was not given.
items.why: A live example of restructuring and white-collar job cuts, a core area for HR transformation work.

items.title: UK chip startup Fractile raises $720M
items.summary: British AI chip startup Fractile closed a $720 million Series C backed by the UK's Sovereign AI Fund, TechCrunch reported on 11 November. The Financial Times put its valuation at $7 billion, up from about $1.1 billion six months earlier; reports of Anthropic interest as a customer are unconfirmed.
items.why: Shows how capital is flowing into AI hardware, and how fast valuations and talent demand can move.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on 10 November, pitching it as its most powerful model for deep, multi-step tasks. Details come from an AI news aggregator and should be treated as provisional until checked against Google's own post.
items.why: New model generations change which knowledge-work tasks get automated, and what skills employers screen for.

items.title: Gemini for Healthcare opens US preview with Northwell and Stanford
items.summary: Google Cloud opened a US preview of Gemini for Healthcare on 10 November, with health systems including Northwell Health and Stanford School of Medicine as launch partners, according to an AI news digest.
items.why: Healthcare is a large AI adoption test case for change management and workforce redesign.

items.title: Adobe adds AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly
items.summary: Adobe announced new AI agents across Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly this week, an AI news roundup reports. Spotify separately added new voice options to its AI DJ for Premium listeners.
items.why: Creative AI agents change how marketing teams produce content and what skills they hire for.

items.title: Report: Chinese army-linked university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite blacklist
items.summary: Reuters reported, as summarised by Techmeme, that a Chinese university with ties to the army bought Nvidia H200 chips despite being on a US export blacklist. No official response was included in the summary.
items.why: Export-control gaps could tighten chip rules, affecting AI costs and tech supply chains.

items.title: COP31 runs 9 to 20 November in Antalya
items.summary: The 2026 UN climate conference is co-led by Türkiye and Australia; the second week, after leaders leave, is where negotiators settle the text.
items.why: Useful context for ESG and sustainability questions in interviews.

items.title: RBI repo rate is 5.50%
items.summary: The MPC raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% in October, its first hike since February 2023, and meets next on 2 to 4 December.
items.why: A key number for any discussion of credit, EMIs and consumer demand.

items.title: Nifty's record high is 26,328.6
items.summary: The Nifty set its lifetime high on 2 January 2026; the Sensex peak is 85,836.1 from 26 September 2024.
items.why: Handy reference when reading market headlines.
